sources: dossier=Intentional absences (2026-05-17, sensor-messaging-unification, rejection): "No advisory-lock-per-subscription / publisher HA primitives in rimsky" and "No sensor-cron per-watch advisory lock" — explicitly supersedes the earlier post-data-platform-cleanup framing; doc=advisory-lock.md line 19 listed Adjacent: `sensor` (scheduler-tick lock); code=the tick lock's only consumer is the scheduler (lib/graph/scheduler/scheduler.go TrySchedulerTick call), sensor.md never mentions tick/advisory locks and states single-replica/no-coordination, and sensor-cron/replica_posture_test.go mechanically fails any sensor source naming an advisory-lock primitive.
note: The sensor adjacency is residue from the retired sensor-coordination design the dossier explicitly rejects; claim-handle.md and message.md are the concepts that actually cite the scheduler-tick lock, so replaced `sensor` with `message` in the Adjacent list (claim-handle was already present).

sources: dossier=no entry claims the never-reuse property is documented at the key definition site; the dossier only establishes the two pinned keys exist (Required behaviors bullet 1, corroborated 2026-05-04/2026-06-08); doc=advisory-lock.md line 28 claimed the property was 'documented as never reuse at the definition site'; code=lib/foundation/persistence/postgres/advisory_locker.go:19-23 declares both keys as bare consts with zero documentation (Plumbline forbids the comment that would have carried it), and no name/assertion/test expresses the property anywhere.
note: The doc's claim about where the never-reuse property is documented is false (no comment can exist there under Plumbline, and none does) and also violates the design-doc self-containment rule by pointing at a code location; rewrote the invariant to state the property itself without the false/self-containment-violating location claim.

sources: dossier="SQLite multi-process safety: bare read-then-write call sites are transactional (immediate-mode transactions), and the scheduler-tick + migration locks are flock-based" (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability, artifact) corroborates that per-name/per-scope locks are subsumed rather than real under SQLite; doc=advisory-lock.md line 26 stated the tx-scoped/COMMIT-ROLLBACK claim unqualified while sibling bullets at lines 23 and 25 both carry explicit (Postgres)/(SQLite) qualifiers, and the doc's own "What it is" paragraph already says the per-name/per-scope locks are SQLite no-ops; code=lib/foundation/persistence/sqlite/advisory_locker.go TakeNamedLockInTx and TakeClaimScopeLockInTx are bare `return nil`.
note: The invariant bullet was inconsistent with its own siblings' qualification style and, read alone, implied a real transaction-scoped lock exists under SQLite; added the (Postgres)/no-op-under-SQLite qualifier to match sibling bullets and the doc's own "What it is" section.
